page: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading running at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and network connectivity is supported by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The server achieves top-tier status in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Multi-threaded performance is highly competitive, with top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks ranks in the top 10 percent, while large block read and write operations fall within the top 25 percent. For database workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, alongside high static web serving throughput.

While multi-core and vector-heavy workloads excel due to advanced instruction support like AVX-512 and AMX, single-core CPU performance remains in the average tier. Prompt processing for large language models ranks in the top tier, but text generation speeds are average. Given the high compute density, fast DDR5 memory, and substantial local NVMe storage, this instance is highly suited for high-performance computing, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server designed for high-throughput workloads. It is powered by a 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of fast 7 GHz DDR5 memory and 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier performance in multi-core benchmarks, software compilation, and database operations. It features advanced hardware acceleration flags, including AVX-512 and AMX, which drive top-tier results in cryptographic tasks and LLM prompt processing. Although single-core performance and text generation speeds are average, its high memory bandwidth and substantial local storage make it highly efficient for demanding multi-threaded applications, large-scale databases, and intensive computational workloads.
